title: WARP: Optics, Holograms, and Worldlines over Shared Causal History
description: Paper VII in the AIΩN Foundations series. This paper defines WARP as an optic architecture over witnessed shared causal history. A WARP optic places an observer-relative aperture over a bounded slice of causal history, lowers the resulting weave under an admissibility law, and retains a holographic witness sufficient for replay, audit, transport, and bounded revelation. The paper argues that WARP is closed over its own witness-bearing outputs: receipts, shells, and certificates are first-class objects for later folding, revelation, comparison, or reliance. It further shows that distributed transport does not introduce a second admission law: transport constructs a comparable slice; once comparable, the same downstream optic applies locally and remotely.
